ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r11.claim: Lot's account does not repeat a call to worship God because he belonged to Abraham's people and Abraham had already made monotheism famous; Abraham and Shuʿayb had to call later peoples to worship God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r11.anchor: ولم يأت في قصة لوط أنه دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r14.claim: وتقطعون السبيل is explained as ending procreation through anal sex, deterring travelers, robbery and murder, or ruining trade through their notoriety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p353/r14.anchor: وتقطعون السبيل: الولد، بتعطيل الفرج ووطء أدبار الرجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r1.claim: نادي means a meeting place and is generic because the towns had many; strictly it is called a club only while its people are assembled, and afterward only figuratively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r1.anchor: وتأتون في ناديكم: أي في مجلسكم الذي تجتمعون فيه، وهو اسم جنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r2.claim: المنكر is whatever reason, religious law, or good character condemns; reported acts include pelting people with pebbles and mocking an unfamiliar stranger, with a report from Umm Hāni tracing to the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r2.anchor: والمنكر: ما تنكره العقول والشرائع والمروءات، حذف الناس بالحصباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r3.speaker: منصور ومجاهد والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة بن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r3.claim: They explain the public wrongdoing as men having intercourse in their gathering where others could watch.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r3.anchor: قاله منصور ومجاهد والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة بن زيد أو تضارطهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists farting and clapping in the assembly as further meanings of the wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r4.anchor: أو تضارطهم أو تصافعهم فيها، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r5.claim: Mujāhid also lists pigeon play, henna on fingertips, whistling, pebble play, and abandoning modesty in all their conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r5.anchor: أو لعب الحمام أو تطريف الأصابع بالحناء، والصفير، والحذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also names pebble-shooting, finger-popping, gum chewing, using a toothstick in public, unfastening clothes, obscene joking, and other indecencies alongside idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r6.anchor: قاله ابن عباس أيضا مع شركهم بالله. كانت فيهم ذنوب غير الفاحشة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r7.claim: Their other wrongs included mutual oppression, backgammon and chess, conspicuous dyed clothing, men dressing as women, and levies on every traveler; they were first to practice male and female same-sex intercourse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r7.anchor: ولعب بالنرد والشطرنج، ولبس المصبغات، ولباس النساء للرجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r8.claim: After Lot exposed these vices, his people persisted in denial and demanded punishment while convinced his warning was false.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p354/r8.anchor: أصروا على اللجاج في التكذيب، فكان جوابهم له: أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.claim: For خير مقاما both vowels denote a place to dwell; النادي and الندي likewise mean an assembly, as al-Ankabut 29:29 and a line by Kathir show.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.anchor: فأما المقام فيمن ضم، وفيمن فتح على اسم المكان، وليس اسم الحدث، ويدل على ذلك:

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r1.claim: Razi says the verse indicates a required hadd for male same-sex intercourse: it shares the label 'abomination' with zina in 17:32, so the deterrent prescribed there applies by analogy.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r1.anchor: ولا تقربوا الزنى إنه كان فاحشة

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r2.claim: He gives a second argument for the hadd: Lot's people were punished with a rain of stones, so perpetrators should receive stoning as an immediate punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r2.anchor: وهو أن الله جعل عذاب من أتى بها إمطار الحجارة

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r5.claim: They satisfy desire with men and abandon the customary way with women, which serves the preservation of human life; this makes the act's obscenity plain, unlike intercourse with women, whose purpose can obscure its wrong.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r5.anchor: يعنى تقضون الشهوة بالرجال مع قطع السبيل المعتاد مع النساء المشتمل على المصلحة التي هي بقاء النوع

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r6.claim: Their wrongdoing adds public display to the ugliness of the act itself.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r6.anchor: يعني ما كفاكم قبح فعلكم حتى تضمون إليه قبح الإظهار

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r7.claim: Razi contrasts Lot's people's challenge with Abraham's people's threat: Abraham attacked their religion and idols by listing their defects, which they found so offensive that they threatened killing and burning him; Lot condemned conduct they did not regard as religious duty.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r7.anchor: والقدح في الدين صعب ، فجعلوا جزاءه القتل والتحريق

RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r8.claim: Lot's people first challenged him to bring punishment because they denied that God would punish them; after he persisted in admonition, they told him to expel his family, as narrated in 27:56.
RAZI-FULL:v25p52/r8.anchor: ثم لما كثر منه ذلك ولم يسكت عنهم قالوا أخرجوا

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r6.claim: Lot challenges them for having sex with men.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r6.anchor: بمردان بطريق مباشرت وآن كار زشت ميكنيد

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r7.claim: A sabil is a customary, easily traversed road; cutting the road can mean travel itself or robbing travelers, which stops people from using it.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r7.anchor: السبيل من الطرق ما هو معتاد السلوك وفيه سهولة وقطع الطريق يقال على وجهين

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r8.claim: One explanation is that they sexually assaulted strangers, often forcing outsiders, until people stopped passing through their town.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r8.anchor: والمعنى تتعرضون لأبناء السبيل بالفاحشة حتى انقطع الناس عن طريقكم. روي : أنهم كانوا كثيرا ما يفعلونها بالغرباء

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r9.claim: Other explanations are highway robbery through killing and taking money to keep people out, or cutting off procreation by abandoning intercourse for farming and having sex with men.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r9.anchor: أو تقطعونها بالقتل وأخذ المال وكانوا يفعلون ذلك لكيلا يدخلوا في بلدهم

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r10.claim: Their nadi is their gathering and conversation hall; it is called a club only while its people are present.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r10.anchor: {في ناديكم} في مجلسكم ومتحدثكم الجامع لأصحابكم فإنه لا يقال النادي والندى إلا لما فيه أهله

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r11.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r11.claim: Kashf al-Asrar defines the nadi as a people's gathering for evening conversation and sociability, with andiya as its plural.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r11.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : النادي مجمع القوم للسمر والإنس وجمعه أندية

BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r12.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r12.claim: Al-Raghib says munkar is whatever sound reason judges vile, or what reason hesitates to condemn but the Sacred Law judges vile.
BURSEVI:v6p336#4/r12.anchor: قال الراغب : المنكر كل شيء تحكم العقول الصحيحة بقبحه أو تتوقف في استقباحه العقول وتحكم بقبحه الشريعة

BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r1.speaker: سفيان الثوري
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r1.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says playing with pigeons was among the practices of Lot's people, and anyone who plays with flying pigeons will taste poverty before dying.
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r1.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري أنه قال : كان اللعب بالحمام من عمل قوم لوط وإن من لعب بالحمام الطيارة

BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r2.claim: When Lot denounced their vices, they mocked him and demanded the punishment he warned would fall if he was truthful.
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r2.anchor: {فما كان جواب قومه} لما أنكر عليهم قبائحهم {إلا أن قالوا} له استهزاء

BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r3.claim: Al-Irshad says this was their only reply at this stage of Lot's warnings; the responses cited at 7:39 and 27:56 came after this exchange, in their final round of disputation.
BURSEVI:v6p337#2/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : فما كان جواب من جهتهم بشيء من الأشياء إلا هذه الكلمة الشنيعة

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r9.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r9.claim: Here the indecency specifically means sex between men; commentators say no people before Lot’s people committed it so widely.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r9.anchor: a transgression that, based upon this verse, commentators say no people had committed on such a wide scale before Lot’s people (IK; cf. 7:81)

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r10.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r10.claim: Given the aggressive approaches described in other accounts, some maintain that Lot reproaches the men for forcible rather than consensual sex.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r10.anchor: some maintain that Lot reproaches them for forcible rather than consensual sexual relations.

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r11.claim: The emphasis in this verse and parallels is on approaching men with desire and lust, whether the relations are consensual or not.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r11.anchor: However, the emphasis here and in 7:81; 26:165–66, and 27:54 is upon approaching men with desire and lust, whether consensual or not

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r12.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r12.claim: “Cutting off the way” can mean that preferring men over women blocks the way to having children.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r12.anchor: preferring men over women means they cut off the way to having children (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r13.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r13.claim: Alternatively, they cut off travelers’ way; some accounts say they specifically targeted travelers for rape.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r13.anchor: or they cut off the way of travelers, as, according to some accounts, they specifically targeted travelers to rape them(Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:29:26/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r14.claim: The people’s challenge to Lot resembles challenges made by the ʿĀd to Hūd and the Thamūd to Ṣāliḥ.
STUDYQURAN:29:26/r14.anchor: Their challenge to Lot is similar to the one the ʿĀd pose to the prophet Hūd

TAB-FULL:v18p388/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains Lot’s accusations as sex with men and assault on strangers who passed through the town.
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r1.anchor: هو ابن السبيل قطعوا به، وعملوا به ذلك العمل الخبيث

TAB-FULL:v18p388/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r2.claim: They waylay travelers and strangers passing through their land to commit their vile act against them.
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r2.anchor: من المسافرين، ومن ورد بلادهم من الغرباء.

TAB-FULL:v18p388/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the road is the travelers’ route: the people intercepted passersby and subjected them to the vile act.
TAB-FULL:v18p388/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {وتقطعون السبيل} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: السبيل: الطريق.

TAB-FULL:v18p389/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r1.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the people used to fart in their meeting places.
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r1.anchor: عن عائشة، في قوله " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: الضراط "

TAB-FULL:v18p389/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r2.claim: In a report from Umm Hāniʾ, the Prophet says they pelted road users and mocked them.
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r2.anchor: عن أم هانئ، قالت: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: «كانوا يخذفون أهل الطريق ويسخرون منهم

TAB-FULL:v18p389/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says they harmed travelers by pelting whoever passed them.
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r3.anchor: قال: سمعت عكرمة، يقول في قوله " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: كانوا يؤذون أهل الطريق، يخذفون من مر بهم "

TAB-FULL:v18p389/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says they pelted everyone who passed them, and that was the wrongdoing.
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r4.anchor: عن السدي، " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: كان كل من مر بهم خذفوه، فهو المنكر "

TAB-FULL:v18p389/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation is that they committed sexual indecency in their gatherings.
TAB-FULL:v18p389/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل كان ذلك إتيانهم الفاحشة في مجالسهم.

TAB-FULL:v18p392/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r1.claim: Mujahid says the men had intercourse with one another in their meeting places.
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " كان يأتي بعضهم بعضا في مجالسهم

TAB-FULL:v18p392/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r2.claim: Qatada says they committed sexual indecency in their gathering.
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: كانوا يأتون الفاحشة في ناديهم "

TAB-FULL:v18p392/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says their gathering was their meeting place and the wrongdoing was their vile assault on riders they intercepted.
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] قال: ناديهم: المجالس، والمنكر: عملهم الخبيث الذي كانوا يعملونه

TAB-FULL:v18p392/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ناديكم as “in your gatherings.”
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] يقول: في مجالسكم "

TAB-FULL:v18p392/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that they pelted passersby in their gatherings and mocked them, based on the report from the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v18p392/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معناه: وتحذفون في مجالسكم المارة بكم، وتسخرون منهم

TAB-FULL:v18p393/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p393/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p393/r1.claim: When Lot prohibited the indecencies God had forbidden, his people answered only by demanding the threatened punishment if he was truthful.

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r5.claim: The emphatic lām and nūn mark a question about conduct no sensible listener would credit or accept.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r5.anchor: استفهام من أمر من الحري أن لا يصدقه سامع ولا يقبله ذو لب ولذا أكد بالنون واللام

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r6.claim: The context points to abandoning the path of procreation by choosing men instead of women; cutting the road is a figure for turning away from women and marriage.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r6.anchor: إهمال طريق التناسل وإلغاؤها وهي إتيان النساء

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r7.claim: A النادي is a meeting place only when its people are gathered; the people of Lot publicly committed sexual obscenities or their vile preliminaries there.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r7.anchor: والنادي هو المجلس الذي يجتمعون فيه ولا يسمى ناديا إلا إذا كان فيه أهله

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r8.claim: A reported alternative says they robbed and assaulted travelers passing their town, pelting them, taking property, having sex with them, and charging three dirhams; another says simply that they were highway robbers. The author says the context contradicts this.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد بقطع السبيل قطع سبيل المارة بديارهم فإنهم كانوا يفعلون هذا الفعل بالمجتازين

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r9.claim: Another view lists many vices in their assemblies, including insults, gambling, pelting passersby, music, nudity, and sodomy; al-Tabataba'i says context indicates the specific sexual conduct already described.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد بإتيان المنكر في النادي أن مجالسهم كانت تشتمل على أنواع المنكرات والقبائح

TABATABAI:29:28-29/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r10.claim: Their sarcastic demand for God's punishment mocks Lot and shows that he had warned them of a punishment; another passage in their story says so.
TABATABAI:29:28-29/r10.anchor: ويظهر من جوابهم أنه كان ينذرهم بعذاب الله

TABATABAI:29:14-40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r2.speaker: جابر
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r2.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur cites Ibn Mardawayh from Jabir: the Prophet forbade khadhf, identifying it with the wrongdoing in Lot's people's council.
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نهى عن الخذف وهو قول الله

TABATABAI:29:14-40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r3.claim: The same explanation is reported through several compilers from Umm Hani: Lot's people sat by the road pelting passersby and mocking them.
TABATABAI:29:14-40/r3.anchor: عن أم هاني بنت أبي طالب ولفظ الحديث قالت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن قول الله

TABRISI:29:29-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r1.claim: The indecency is men having sex with men.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r1.anchor: ثم فسر الفاحشة بقوله { إنكم لتأتون الرجال } أي تنكحونهم

TABRISI:29:29-30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r2.claim: One explanation is that preferring men to women cuts off procreation.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r2.anchor: أحدها: تقطعون سبيل الولد باختياركم الرجال على النساء

TABRISI:29:29-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r3.claim: A second account says they attacked passing travelers: they stoned them by lot, seized the person hit, took his property, sodomized him, charged three dirhams, and had a judge rule on it.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r3.anchor: وثانيها: إنكم تقطعون الناس عن الأسفار بإتيان هذه الفاحشة

TABRISI:29:29-30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r4.claim: A third explanation is that they robbed people on the road like highway bandits.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r4.anchor: وثالثها: إنهم كانوا يقطعون الطريق على الناس كما يفعل قطاع الطريق

TABRISI:29:29-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وروي عن الرضا
TABRISI:29:29-30/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, with a report also from al-Riḍā, says they farted in their gatherings without modesty or shame.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r5.anchor: أحدها: هو أنهم كانوا يتضارطون في مجالسهم من غير حشمة ولا حياء

TABRISI:29:29-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:29:29-30/r6.claim: Mujāhid says they had sex with men in their assemblies in full view of one another.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r6.anchor: وثانيها: أنهم كانوا يأتون الرجال في مجالسهم يرى بعضهم بعضا عن مجاهد

TABRISI:29:29-30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r7.claim: A third view lists public indecencies: insults, buffoonery, slapping, gambling, stick-fighting, stone-throwing, music, exposure, and sodomy.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r7.anchor: كانت مجالسهم تشتمل على أنواع من المناكير والقبائح مثل الشتم والسخف والصفع

TABRISI:29:29-30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:29:29-30/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj draws a lesson: people should not socialize around indecencies or gather to commit forbidden acts.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: وفي هذا إعلام أنه لا ينبغي أن يتعاشر الناس على المناكير

TABRISI:29:29-30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:29-30/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:29-30/r9.claim: When Lot condemned their disgraceful acts, they mocked him by demanding God’s punishment; Lot then prayed for help against the corrupt people who committed sins and spread corruption.
TABRISI:29:29-30/r9.anchor: ولما أنكر لوط على قومه ما كانوا يأتونه من الفضائح قالوا له استهزاء ائتنا بعذاب الله

THALABI:v7p277#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p277#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p277#2/r1.claim: The Prophet warns against flicking small stones: it neither harms an enemy nor catches game, but can blind an eye or break a tooth.
THALABI:v7p277#2/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إياكم والخذف فإنه لا ينكأ العدو

THALABI:v7p277#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p277#2/r2.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
THALABI:v7p277#2/r2.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad identifies the assembly's wrongdoing as farting; they used to fart in their gatherings.
THALABI:v7p277#2/r2.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر قال: الضراط، كانوا يتضارطون في مجالسهم

THALABI:v7p277#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p277#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p277#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says they had sex with one another in their assemblies.
THALABI:v7p277#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان يجامع بعضهم بعضا في مجالسهم

THALABI:v7p277#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p277#2/r4.speaker: مكحول
THALABI:v7p277#2/r4.claim: Makhul lists ten traits of Lot's people found in this community, including gum chewing, henna on fingers, loosened waistcloths, finger practices, a wrapped turban, saliniyya, pellet throwing, whistling, khadhf, and same-sex acts.
THALABI:v7p277#2/r4.anchor: عن مكحول، قال: عشرة في هذه الأمة من أخلاق قوم لوط: مضغ العلك، وتطويق الأصابع بالحناء، وحل الإزار

THALABI:v7p277#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p277#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p277#2/r5.claim: They demand punishment because Lot had threatened them with it; the commentary says the punishment is indeed coming upon them.
THALABI:v7p277#2/r5.anchor: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين إنه نازل بنا وذلك إنه أوعدهم العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they blocked the road to travelers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: الطريق على المار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r2.claim: Muqātil says they pelted passersby with sling-thrown stones, thereby stopping travelers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وذلك أنهم يرمون ابن السبيل الحجارة بالخذف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they did this to travelers passing by and to strangers who came to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد في ذلك: إنهم كانوا يفعلون ذلك لمن مر بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Lot’s people sat in gatherings with pebbles and claimed any traveler hit; Ibn ʿAbbās says people then avoided their route.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r4.anchor: روي عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في تفسير هذه الآية: "أن قوم لوط كانوا يجلسون في مجالسهم، وعند كل رجل منهم قصعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says they intercepted people on the roads to commit their sexual vice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء في قوله: {وتقطعون السبيل} قطعه أنهم كانوا يعترضون الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj reports another interpretation: they cut off the path of offspring.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p517#2/r6.anchor: وحكى الزجاج قولا آخر؛ فقال: جاء في التفسير: وتقطعون سبيل الولد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines the nādī as an assembly or council and refers to Maryam 19:73 for discussion of the word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} النادي: المجلس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says sexual immorality became entrenched among them, so they committed it with one another in their gatherings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: استمكنت الفاحشة فيهم حتى فعل بعضهم ببعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies their indecency as intercourse with men.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r4.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r4.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad says their indecency was farting in their gatherings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r4.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد: هو الضراط؛ كانوا يتضارطون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r5.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r5.claim: Asked by Umm Hāniʾ about their public indecency, the Prophet said they stoned travelers and mocked them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r5.anchor: وروي أن أم هانئ سألت رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- عن المنكر الذي كانوا يأتونه في ناديهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r6.claim: Muqātil identifies the public indecency as pelting people with stones.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r6.anchor: وهو قول مقاتل في تفسير المنكر؛ يعني: الخذف بالحجارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines indecency as a gathering of obscene speech and actions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: المنكر: مجمع الفواحش من القول والفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq draws a lesson that people should gather around what brings them near God, not around wrongdoing, mockery, or idle amusement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r8.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أعلم الله -عز وجل- أنه لا ينبغي أن يتعاشر الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r9.claim: When Lot warned them of punishment unless they believed, they mockingly challenged him to bring it if he was truthful that it would descend on them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p519/r9.anchor: قالوا له استهزاء: {ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين} أن العذاب نازل بنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r1.claim: One explanation is that they cut off the possibility of having children; another says they seize travelers on the road to solicit sexual immorality.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r1.anchor: أي: سبيل الولد. وقيل: يأخذون الناس من الطرق لطلب الفاحشة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r2.claim: Their wrongdoing in their gathering was that they had intercourse with one another.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r2.anchor: في ناديكم } مجلسكم { المنكر } كان بعضهم يجامع بعضا في مجالسهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r3.claim: His people answer by demanding the punishment he says will come upon them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:29/r3.anchor: قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين } أنه نازل بنا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r5.claim: The rhetorical question refers to men having intercourse with men in their rear.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r5.anchor: {ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين {28} أئنكم لتأتون الرجال} [العنكبوت: 28-29] في أدبارهم، وهذا على الاستفهام، أي: أنكم تفعلون ذلك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r6.claim: They attacked the road by waylaying outsiders, assaulting them sexually and seizing them; they did this to strangers rather than one another.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r6.anchor: قال: {وتقطعون السبيل} [العنكبوت: 29] على الغرباء، فتأتونهم في أدبارهم، وكانوا لا يفعلون ذلك إلا بالغرباء، وكانوا يتعرضون الطرق، ويأخذون الغرباء ولا يفعله بعضهم ببعض.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r7.claim: Their evil in their gathering means committing that indecency in their assembly.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p626#2/r7.anchor: قال: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] في مجمعكم والمنكر الفاحشة، يعني: فعلهم ذلك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p627/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p627/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p627/r1.claim: Lot’s people challenged him to bring the punishment he had been warning them about.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p627/r1.anchor: {فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين} [العنكبوت: 29] وذلك لما كان يعدهم به من العذاب.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r1.claim: The account of Lot and his people repeats material treated in earlier sūras, where the commentary has already provided related explanations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r1.anchor: önceki bazı sûrelerde de yeri geldikçe birbirine yakın ifadelerle verilmiştir; ayrıca oralarda konuyla ilgili gerekli açıklama ve yorumları da sunmuş bulunuyoruz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r2.claim: God made natural reproduction and sexual life depend on union between male and female.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r2.anchor: Allah Teâlâ varlık düzeni içinde doğal üremeyi ve cinsel hayatı erkekle dişi arasındaki birleşmeye bağlamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r3.claim: Lot clearly taught that the only lawful sexual relationship for men is marriage to women.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r3.anchor: Hz. Lût, erkekler için tek meşrû ilişki yolunun kadınlarla evlenme olduğunu açıkça belirtmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r4.claim: The relevant passages prohibit homosexuality in unequivocal terms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r4.anchor: aynı yerlerde eşcinsellik kesin bir dille yasaklanmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r5.claim: The community was warned that widespread immorality would bring a severe catastrophe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:28/r5.anchor: bu ahlâksızlığın yaygınlık kazandığı toplumu bekleyen âkıbetin ağır bir felâket olduğu bildirilmiştir

SULAMI:v2p116#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r1.claim: Asked about the verse, al-Junayd says any gathering people hold together for something other than remembrance is an evil.
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r1.anchor: سئل الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : عن هذه الآية قال : كل شيء يجتمع عليه الناس إلا الذكر فهو منكر

SULAMI:v2p116#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir interprets the evil as failing to enjoin right and forbid wrong.
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : لا تأمرون بالمعروف ولا تنهون عن المنكر

SULAMI:v2p116#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r3.speaker: القيم
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r3.claim: Al-Qayyim interprets the evil as neglecting the respect owed to elders.
SULAMI:v2p116#2/r3.anchor: قال القيم : المنكر هو ترك حرمة الأكابر

ITQAN:v4p523#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p523#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p523#4/r1.claim: Umm Hani asked the Prophet what the people did in their club; he said they pelted and mocked travelers. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
ITQAN:v4p523#4/r1.anchor: أخرج أحمد والترمذي وحسنه وغيرهما عن أم هانيء قالت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله ﴿ وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p385/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r5.claim: Cutting off the road means terrorizing travelers; another view says the phrase refers to sodomy.
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r5.anchor: الثالث : القطع إخافة السبيل قوله تعالى في سورة العنكبوت

DAMGHANI:v1p385/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r6.claim: An alternative interpretation takes “cutting off the road” to mean sodomy.
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r6.anchor: يعني يخيفون وقيل هو اللواط الرابع : القطع ترك حق الأقارب

DAMGHANI:v1p15/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r1.claim: Atā can mean to do or commit; the people of Lot commit the objectionable act in their gathering.
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r1.anchor: الإتيان العمل قوله عز وجل في سورة العنكبوت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r5.claim: Qaṭʿ can mean waylaying or intimidating travelers on a route.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r5.anchor: والثالث : اخافة السبيل . ومنه قوله تعالى في العنكبوت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r7.claim: A sixth sense is doing or committing an act, as in committing something objectionable in one’s gathering.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r7.anchor: والسادس : العمل . ومنه قوله تعالى في العنكبوت :

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r1.claim: Nādī means an assembly or gathering place.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r2.claim: Al-munkar here is a gathering of obscenities in speech and action; interpreters disagree about which specific wrongdoing is meant.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#3/r2.anchor: و"المنكر" مجمع الفواحش من القول والفعل. وقد اختلف في ذلك المنكر.

NAHHAS:v3p254/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p254/r4.speaker: قراءة الكوفيين
NAHHAS:v3p254/r4.claim: The Kufan reading interrogates the first and second occurrences; Abū ʿAmr does likewise but lightens the hamza.
NAHHAS:v3p254/r4.anchor: في الأولى والثانية على الاستفهام وكذا قراءة أبي عمرو إلا أنه يخفف

NAHHAS:v3p254/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p254/r5.speaker: نافع
NAHHAS:v3p254/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the first occurrence without interrogation and interrogates the second; this follows the written form and is an emphatic challenge rather than a question.
NAHHAS:v3p254/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع ( إنكم ) بغير استفهام في الأولى واستفهم في الثانية وهذه القراءة على اتباع السواد

NAHHAS:v3p254/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p254/r6.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p254/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd compares this emphatic, non-interrogative reading with the poet's exchange: they asked whether he loved her, and he answered certainly.
NAHHAS:v3p254/r6.anchor: وكذا قال محمد بن يزيد في قول الشاعر

NAHHAS:v3p254/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p254/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v3p254/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd considers the first reading remote because it places two interrogatives together.
NAHHAS:v3p254/r7.anchor: القراءة الأولى عند أبي عبيد بعيدة للجمع بين الاستفهامين

NAHHAS:v3p254/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p254/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p254/r8.claim: The author rejects Abū ʿUbayd's objection: a question may follow a question, and the comparison he cites from this sūra is unlike this construction.
NAHHAS:v3p254/r8.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وليس الأمر كذلك لأن هذا استفهام بعد استفهام وليس ينكر في مثل هذا استفهامان

ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r1.claim: The wording is formally a question but functions as assertion and rebuke.
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r1.anchor: اللفظ لفظ استفهام، والمعنى معنى التقرير والتوبيخ

ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r2.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r2.claim: One view says they obstructed the path of offspring; another says they intercepted travelers for sexual immorality.
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير ويقطعون سبيل الولد

ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r3.claim: One report says they pelted and mocked people in gatherings; God calls this wrongdoing and forbids socializing around mockery.
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r3.anchor: قيل إنهم كانوا يخذفون الناس في مجالسهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r4.claim: People should gather for what brings them nearer to God and farther from His displeasure, not mockery or amusement.
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r4.anchor: ولا يجتمعوا إلا فيما قرب إلى الله

ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p168/r5.claim: Another view is that they committed sexual immorality in their gatherings.

ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r1.speaker: Baghawi and Zamakhshari (on Al-Hasan's authority)
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r1.claim: Baghawi and Zamakhshari, citing Al-Hasan, advance the reading that the phrase means cutting across the way of nature.
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r1.anchor: advanced by Baghawi and (on the authority of Al-Hasan) by Zamakhshari

ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r2.claim: Razi adopts the same interpretation exclusively and without reservation.
ASAD-NOTES:29:28#n24/r2.anchor: Razi adopts it exclusively and without reservation

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f7.claim: Al-Ankabut details the people's offenses, including coming to men, cutting the road, and public indecency; Hud compresses their behavior as doing evil deeds, suiting the longer account.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f7.anchor: ففصل في عمل السيئات ما لم يفصله في هود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r2.claim: Ankabut lists Lot's people's specific sins—sex with men, cutting off the road, and evil in their gatherings—whereas Hud only summarizes their evil deeds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r2.anchor: وذكر تعالى من صفات قوم لوط السيئة (وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r3.claim: Lot's distress and anticipation of rescue are greater in Ankabut: his people demand punishment and he prays for help, so he experiences the messengers' arrival as prolonged; this also makes أن apt, possibly as emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p922/r3.anchor: برِم لوط وضيقه بقومه كان أكثر فكأنه استبطأ مجيء العذاب على هؤلاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir interrogates without lengthening the hamza; Nafi is reported both with madd and with Ibn Kathir's form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r2.anchor: وكان ابن كثير يستفهم بغير مد، يلفظ بياء بعد الألف، [وروي عن نافع المد، وروي] عنه مثل قراءة ابن كثير.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وابن ذكوان
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r3.claim: Ibn Amir and Ibn Dhakwan read the interrogative with two hamzas, with length between them in the reported form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r3.anchor: وكان ابن عامر يهمز همزتين في أإنكم، وقال ابن ذكوان عنه بهمزتين والاستفهام،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r4.claim: Hafs matches Nafi's first occurrence and reads the second with two hamzas.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r4.anchor: حفص عن عاصم في الأول مثل نافع الثاني بهمزتين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r5.claim: These readers make both occurrences interrogative; Abu Amr does not use two hamzas, while the others do.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p431#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي بالاستفهام فيهما غير أن أبا عمرو لا يهمز همزتين، وهؤلاء يهمزون همزتين .

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p280/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p280/r1.claim: Both clauses may be interrogative, or the first declarative and second interrogative; the hamzas may both be clear or the second softened. The author refers to earlier explanations.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p280/r1.anchor: يقرآن معا بالاستفهام ويقرأ الأول بالاخبار والثاني بالاستفهام وبتحقيق الهمزتين معا وبتحقيق الأولى وتليين الثانية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r1.claim: Nafi is reported with a lengthened form of أئنكم; another report gives his reading like Ibn Kathir's.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r1.anchor: ويروى عن نافع المد / آينكم لتأتون الرجال / ويروى عنه مثل قراءة ابن كثير

IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r2.claim: Hafs and Ibn ʿĀmir read أئنكم with two hamzas; Ibn ʿĀmir transmitters differ over lengthening between them.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r2.anchor: وحفص عن عاصم يهمز همزتين فى ﴿ أئنكم لتأتون ﴾ وكان ابن عامر يهمز همزتين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r3.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r3.claim: A report from Hishām gives Ibn ʿĀmir's two hamzas and lengthening, comparing the reading to عائذا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r3.anchor: وإنما قلت ذلك لأن أبا العباس أحمد بن محمد بن بكر أخبرنى عن هشام بن عمار بإسناده عن ابن عامر / آنذا /

IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم عن أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r4.claim: These readers use interrogative forms at both locations; Abu ʿAmr does not pronounce two hamzas, while the others do.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p499/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وحمزة والكسائى بالاستفهام فيهما / أئنكم . . . أئنكم /

NASHR:v1p429/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r1.claim: Hamza easing at pause is well known in Arabic and suits Ḥamza’s otherwise strongly articulated reading; transmitted reports also allow him to pronounce hamza fully in rapid recitation.
NASHR:v1p429/r1.anchor: وقد اختص حمزة بذلك من حيث إن قراءته اشتملت على شدة التحقيق والترتيل والمد والسكت،

NASHR:v1p429/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r2.speaker: سفيان الثوري
NASHR:v1p429/r2.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī said that Ḥamza did not recite any part of God’s Book without transmitted precedent.
NASHR:v1p429/r2.anchor: فقد قال فيه سفيان الثوري: ما قرأ حمزة حرفا من كتاب الله إلا بأثر.

NASHR:v1p429/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r3.speaker: حمران بن أعين وطلحة بن مصرف وجعفر بن محمد والأعمش وسلام بن سليمان وهشام بن عمار وأبو سليمان عن قالون
NASHR:v1p429/r3.claim: Other transmitters also ease hamza at pause: several in general, Hishām in one route for final hamza, and Abū Sulaymān from Qālūn for accusative tanwīn.
NASHR:v1p429/r3.anchor: وقد وافق حمزة على تسهيل الهمزة في الوقف حمران بن أعين، وطلحة بن مصرف، وجعفر بن محمد

NASHR:v1p429/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r4.claim: Hamza is either still or moving; a still hamza may be final or medial, and a final one may be permanent or become still only at pause.
NASHR:v1p429/r4.anchor: الهمز ينقسم إلى ساكن ومتحرك. فالساكن ينقسم إلى متطرف، وهو ما ينقطع الصوت عليه،

NASHR:v1p429/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r5.claim: A permanently still final hamza in the Qurʾān follows fatḥa or kasra, not ḍamma; the source gives examples and notes a ḍamma example only outside the Qurʾān.
NASHR:v1p429/r5.anchor: فالساكن اللازم يأتي قبله مفتوح مثل (اقرأ) ومكسور مثل (نبئ) ولم يأت به في القرآن قبله مضموم،

NASHR:v1p429/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r6.claim: An incidentally still final hamza may follow any of the three vowels, with examples following ḍamma, kasra, and fatḥa.
NASHR:v1p429/r6.anchor: والساكن العارض يأتي قبله الحركات الثلاث، فمثاله وقبله الضم

NASHR:v1p429/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r7.claim: A medial still hamza can be medial in itself after ḍamma, kasra, or fatḥa; the author gives examples for each environment.
NASHR:v1p429/r7.anchor: وأما الساكن المتوسط فينقسم إلى قسمين: متوسط بنفسه ومتوسط بغيره. فالمتوسط بنفسه

NASHR:v1p429/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p429/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p429/r8.claim: When medial by another letter, a hamza preceded by a letter is shown only after fatḥa; when medial by a word, it may follow ḍamma or kasra.
NASHR:v1p429/r8.anchor: والمتوسط بغيره على قسمين: متوسط بحرف، ومتوسط بكلمة. فالمتوسط بحرف يكون قبله فتح

QIRAAT-ER:29:29:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:29:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:29:1#1/r1.claim: This variant changes the realization of the interrogative hamza without changing the meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:29:29:1#1/r1.anchor: Hamza treatment variant — alternative realization of the interrogative hamza, no semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#4/r1.claim: Qatāda explains “in your gathering” as “in your assemblies.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر ﴾ قال في مجالسكم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r1.claim: The first accusation means that they have intercourse with men.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that they stopped travelers by forcing them into the shameful act or having intercourse with them against their will.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r2.anchor: أي وتقطعون الطريق بسبب تكليف الغرباء والمارة تلك الفعلة القبيحة واتيانهم كرها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that they cut off procreation by turning away from women as a field and approaching what is not a field.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r3.anchor: أو وتقطعون سبيل النسل بالاعراض عن الحرث واتيان ما ليس بحرث

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r4.claim: Others interpret cutting the road as highway robbery through murder and taking property, or as ruining their reputation with scandalous stories.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : تقطعون الطريق بالقتل وأخذ المال وقيل : تقطعونه بقبح الاحدوثة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r5.claim: نادي means their meeting place; it is a collective noun because they had many assemblies, and the place is called a gathering only while its people are present.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r5.anchor: أي في مجلسكم الذي تجتمعون فيه وهو اسم جنس إذ أديتهم في مجالسهم كثيرة ولا يسمى ناديا إلا إذا كان فيه أهله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r6.speaker: أم هانئ
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r6.claim: Asked by Umm Hani about the wrongdoing in their assembly, the Prophet said they sat by the road, pelted travelers, and mocked them; al-Tirmidhi graded the report good and al-Hakim authenticated it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r6.anchor: عن أم هانيء بنت أبي طالب قالت : سات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد ومنصور والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r7.claim: Mujahid, Mansur, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say the people openly had intercourse with men in their assemblies.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r7.anchor: وعن مجاهد ومنصور والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة وابن زيد هو اتيان الرجال في مجالسهم يرى بعضهم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r8.claim: Mujahid also identifies the misconduct as pigeon play, henna on the fingers, whistling, stone-throwing, and shameless behavior generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r8.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا هو لعب الحمام وتطريف الاصابع بالحناء والصفير والخذف ونبذ الحياء في جميع أمورهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says they farted and clapped their hands in their gatherings.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هو تضارطهم وتصافعهم فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas lists pebble shooting, slingshots, finger snapping, chewing gum, using a tooth stick publicly, loosening the waist garment, insults, and obscene joking.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r10.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه هو الخذف بالحصى والرمي بالبنادق والفرقعة ومضغ العلك والسواك بين الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r11.claim: Alusi says Lot's people needed no renewed call to worship because Lot lived among Abraham's people and after Abraham's monotheistic preaching had become known; Lot emphasized the distinctive prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r11.anchor: لم يأت في قصة لوط عليه السلام أنه دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله تعالى كما جاء في قصة إبراهيم وكذا في قصة شعيب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r12.claim: By contrast, Abraham and Shuayb came after those who worshipped and called to God had passed away, so each called his people to worship God.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r12.anchor: وأما إبراهيم وشعيب عليهما السلام فجاءا بعد انقراض من كان يعبد الله عز وجل ويدعو اليه سبحانه فلذلك دعا كل منهما قومه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r13.claim: Instead of answering Lot's objections, his people challenged him to bring God's punishment if he was truthful.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#2/r13.anchor: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r1.claim: One reading takes their challenge as demanding the punishment Lot had threatened, implying that he warned them of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r1.anchor: أي فيما تعدنا من نزول العذاب على ما في الكشاف وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r2.claim: Another reading makes them challenge Lot's implied claim that their conduct deserved punishment, conveyed by his reproachful question.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r2.anchor: في دعوى استحقاقنا العذاب على ما نحن عليه المفهومة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r3.claim: A third reading makes their reply challenge Lot's assertion that the conduct he censured was reprehensible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r3.anchor: في دعوى استقباح ذلك الناطق بها كلامك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan, followed by Abu al-Su'ud, places this answer at Lot's first admonition and the expulsion answer in al-A'raf and al-Naml later, so the exclusive formulations do not conflict.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r4.anchor: قاله أبو حيان وتبعه أبو السعود وتعقب بأن هذا التعيين يحتاج إلى توقيف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r5.claim: The chronological account is challenged for lacking transmitted evidence; its defense is that mockery suits early admonition, while expulsion suits later retaliation after repeated reproach.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r5.anchor: من باب التكذيب والسخرية وهو أوفق بأوائل المواعظ والتوبيخات

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r6.claim: Another reconciliation says this answer responds to Lot's counsel, whereas the expulsion answer records what his people said among themselves while deliberating.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r6.anchor: إن ما هنا جواب قومه عليه السلام له إذ نصحهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r7.claim: A further reconciliation assigns the two answers to different groups, one to the chiefs and the other to everyone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r7.anchor: إن أحد الجوابين صدر عن كبار قومه وامرائهم والآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r8.claim: Some eminent commentators appear to choose that each exclusive answer is relative to the response Lot hoped to receive when calling them to follow him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p153#3/r8.anchor: يقتضي اختيار أن يكون كل من الحصرين بالاضافة إلى الجواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r4.claim: They committed the sexual act against travelers who passed them, causing people to stop using the route.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r4.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يفعلون الفاحشة بمن يمر بهم من المسافرين، فترك الناس الممر بهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r5.claim: An alternative explanation is that they cut off procreation by preferring men to women.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: تقطعون سبيل النسل بإيثار الرجال على النساء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r6.claim: Nadi, nada, and muntada all mean the people’s meeting place or gathering where they converse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r6.anchor: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} النادي، والندى، والمنتدى: مجلس القوم ومتحدثهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r7.speaker: أم هانئ
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r7.claim: Umm Hani reports that the Prophet identified the vice as throwing things at passersby and mocking them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r7.anchor: عن أم هانئ] (1) قالت: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r8.claim: They reportedly sat with bowls of pebbles and pelted passing strangers; whoever was hit became the one entitled to that traveler.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r8.anchor: ويروى أنهم كانوا يجلسون في مجالسهم، وعند كل رجل منهم قصعة فيه حصى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r9.claim: Another report says they took a traveler’s belongings, raped him, charged him three dirhams, and had a judge for this practice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان يأخذ ما معه وينكحه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r10.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r10.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad says they passed wind in their gatherings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r10.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد: كانوا يتضارطون في مجالسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r11.claim: Mujahid says they had sex with one another in their gatherings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان يجامع بعضهم بعضا في مجالسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r12.claim: Abdullah ibn Salam says they spat on one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r12.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن سلام قال: كان يبزق بعضهم على بعض.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r13.speaker: مكحول
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r13.claim: Mak’hul lists their habits as chewing gum, decorating fingertips with henna, loosening waist wrappers, whistling, pelting people, and same-sex intercourse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r13.anchor: وعن مكحول قال: كان من أخلاق قوم لوط مضغ العلك وتطريف الأصابع بالحناء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r14.claim: After Lot condemned their abominations, his people mockingly challenged him to bring God’s punishment if he was truthful that it would come.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p239#2/r14.anchor: {فما كان جواب قومه} لما أنكر عليهم لوط ما يأتونه من القبائح، {إلا أن قالوا} له استهزاء: {ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.claim: They have sex with men and cut off the road by attacking travelers, killing and robbing them, or raping them until routes are blocked.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.anchor: وتتعرضون للسابلة بالقتل وأخذ المال أو بالفاحشة حتى انقطعت الطرق

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.claim: Alternatively, they cut off procreation by turning away from women and having sex that cannot produce offspring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.anchor: أو تقطعون سبيل النسل بالإعراض عن الحرث وإتيان ما ليس بحرث

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.claim: A nādī is an assembly while its people are gathered in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.anchor: في مجالسكم الغاصة بأهلها ولا يقال للنادي إلا لما فيه أهله

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.claim: The reprehensible acts include sex, farting, exposing clothing, and other shameless behaviors.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.anchor: كالجماع والضراط وحل الإزار وغيرها من القبائح عدم مبالاة بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.claim: Another view identifies the public misconduct as hذف, throwing small stones or pellets.

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.claim: Their demand for divine punishment challenges either Lot's judgment that their conduct is vile or the prophethood implied by his rebuke.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.anchor: في استقباح ذلك أو في دعوى النبوة المفهومة من التوبيخ

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r6.claim: The repeated rebuke underscores the offense of sex with men; Lot adds their other wrongs to show multiple grounds for blame and continues urging them despite their apparently hopeless corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r6.anchor: ثم كرر الإنكار تأكيدا لتجاوز قبحها الذي ينكرونه فقال : { أئنكم لتأتون الرجال } إتيان الشهوة , وعطف عليها ما ضموه إليها من المناكر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r7.claim: They cut off the road by harming traders and passersby.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r7.anchor: وتقطعون السبيل * } أي بأذى الجلابين والمارة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r8.claim: A nadi is the place where people gather to converse and hear one another; it is called nadi while the group is present, but not after they leave.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r8.anchor: المكان الذي تجلسون فيه للتحدث بحيث يسمع بعضكم نداء بعض من مجلس المؤانسة , وهو ناد ما دام القوم فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r9.claim: Munkar covers acts condemned by revealed law, honorable conduct, and reason, even if the impropriety is slight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r9.anchor: أي هذا الجنس , وهو ما تنكره الشرائع والمروءات والعقول , ولا تتحاشون عن شيء منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r10.claim: They openly commit every kind of wrong together without shame, although people ordinarily avoid even what is less than proper in company.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r10.anchor: في المجتمع الذي يتحاشى فيه الإنسان من فعل خلاف الأولى , من غير أن يستحي بعضكم من بعض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r11.claim: In obstinacy, ignorance, and mockery, they answered the warnings by demanding God's punishment if Lot was truthful; invoking God's greatest name made their insolence worse, and the challenge was meant to provoke him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r11.anchor: إلا أن قالوا } عنادا وجهلا واستهزاء : { ائتنا بعذاب الله } وعبروا بالاسم الأعظم زيادة في الجرأة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r12.claim: Their phrase if you are among the truthful challenges Lot's authority to warn and seeks to inflame and provoke him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r12.anchor: { إن كنت } أي كونا متمكنا { من الصادقين * } أي في وعيدك وإرسالك , إلهابا وتهييجا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r13.claim: Lot turns away from his people and addresses God as his benefactor, asking for help against a powerful, corrupt people beyond his ability to resist.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p554/r13.anchor: معرضا عنهم , مقبلا بكليته على المحسن إليه : { رب } أي أيها المحسن إلي { انصرني على القوم }

DURR-FULL:v6p459/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says Lot's people intercepted travelers on the road and committed their sexual offense against them.
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وتقطعون السبيل} قال: الطريق إذا مر بهم المسافر وهو ابن السبيل قطعوا به

DURR-FULL:v6p459/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r3.claim: The gathering-place (nādī) is glossed as a council or meeting place.
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r3.anchor: في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم} قال: مجلسكم

DURR-FULL:v6p459/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r4.speaker: أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r4.claim: Umm Hani asked the Prophet about the phrase concerning wrongdoing in their assembly; the report is transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, with its answer continuing in the next segment.
DURR-FULL:v6p459/r4.anchor: عن أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب رضي الله عنها قالت: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قول الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r1.claim: In the Umm Hani report begun in the preceding segment, the Prophet explains that they sat by roads, pelted travelers with pebbles, and mocked them.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r1.anchor: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال كانوا يجلسون بالطريق فيخذفون ابن السبيل ويسخرون منهم

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r2.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet prohibited khadhf, citing this verse as describing the practice.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r2.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن الخذف وهو قول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r3.claim: Ibn Umar identifies the wrongdoing as khadhf; when a man challenges him, he throws a handful of pebbles at his face and reproaches him for using equivocation about the Prophet's report.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: الخذف فقال رجل

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the wrongdoing as khadhf, pelting with small stones.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: الخذف

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r5.claim: Ikrima says they used to pelt people in their assemblies.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: كانوا يخذفون الناس

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r6.claim: Mujahid says they practiced intercourse with one another in their assemblies.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: كان يجامع بعضهم بعضا في المجالس

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r7.claim: Qatada says they committed sexual indecency in their assemblies.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال كانوا يعملون الفاحشة في مجالسهم

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r8.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r8.claim: Aisha identifies the wrongdoing as farting.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r8.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: الضراط

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r9.speaker: القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r9.claim: Al-Qasim b. Muhammad says they farted in their assemblies, one at another.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r9.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه سئل عن قول الله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر}

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r10.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r10.claim: The author glosses nādī as a meeting place or assembly.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r10.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه سئل عن قول الله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} ماذا كان المنكر

DURR-FULL:v6p461/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r11.claim: Mujahid lists whistling, pigeon games, jalahq projectiles, and unfastening the buttons of robes as their assembly's wrongdoing.
DURR-FULL:v6p461/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: الصفير ولعب الحمام والجلاهق وحل ازرار القباء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says they cut off travelers who pass them on the road and subject them to the foul act.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r1.anchor: السبيل : الطريق المسافر اذا مر بهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ناديكم as your gathering places.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في ناديكم المنكر يقول : في مجالسكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r3.speaker: رسول الله ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r3.claim: In a report from Umm Hani, the Prophet says their public misdeed was pelting travelers and mocking them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r3.anchor: عن ام هانئ بنت ابي طالب قالت : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، عن قوله : تاتون في ناديكم المنكر قال : كانوا يحذفون اهل الطريق ويسخرون منهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r4.claim: Aisha identifies the misdeed in their gathering as farting.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r4.anchor: عن عائشة في قوله : وتاتون في ناديكم المنكر قالت : الضراط .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r5.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r5.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad says they farted at one another in their meeting place, and نادي means a gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r5.anchor: سئل القاسم بن محمد ، عن قول الله : وتاتون في ناديكم المنكر ما ذاك المنكر ؟ قال : كانوا يتضارطون في المجلس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r6.claim: Mujahid says they had sex with men in their gathering places.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد ياتون في ناديكم المنكر قال : كانوا يجامعون الرجال في مجالسهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r7.claim: Mujahid also identifies the misdeeds as whistling, playing with pigeons and pellet slings, and unfastening the coat buttons.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3054/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد وتاتون في ناديكم المنكر قال : الصفير ولعب الحمام والجلاهق

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3055/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3055/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3055/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains the challenge as referring to what Lot says: if his statement about the punishment is true, it will be as he says.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3055/r1.anchor: عن الربيع ابن انس ، عن ابي العالية يعني قوله : ان كنت من الصادقين بما تقول انه كما تقول .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p239/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p239/r11.speaker: جميع القراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p239/r11.claim: All readers pronounce the corresponding question about approaching men with two hamzas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p239/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجميع { أإنكم لتأتون الرجال } بهمزتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r1.claim: The question about approaching men and the coordinated actions is an appositional expansion of the general charge of indecency; the further offenses are included in that charge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r1.anchor: وجملة { أينكم لتأتون الرجال } الخ بدل اشتمال من مضمون جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r2.claim: The denunciatory question covers the entire list and repeats the emphatic particle so the appositional clause matches its antecedent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r2.anchor: وأدخل استفهام الإنكار على جميع التفصيل وأعيد حرف التأكيد لتتطابق جملة البدل مع الجملة المبدل منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r3.claim: Cutting the road means attacking travelers by taking property, killing them, or coercing them into indecency.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r4.claim: Lot’s people used to sit along the roads to seize whichever passersby they chose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r4.anchor: وكان قوم لوط يقعدون بالطرق ليأخذوا من المارة من يختارونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r5.claim: Road attacks are inherently corrupt and especially corrupt in this aim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r5.anchor: فقطع السبيل فساد في ذاته وهو أفسد في هذا المقصد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r6.claim: They used their gathering to discuss, prepare for, and initiate the indecency, including flirtation and casting pebbles to choose a target; public display worsened it by abandoning concealment and spreading the practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r6.anchor: وأما إتيان المنكر في ناديهم فإنهم جعلوا ناديهم للحديث في ذكر هذه الفاحشة والاستعداد لها ومقدماتها كالتغازل برمي الحصى اقتراعا بينهم على من يرومونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r8.claim: A nādī is the daytime place of gathering, conversation, and consultation, from nadw, assembly by day; a nighttime gathering is a sāmir, and an empty meeting place is not called a nādī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r8.anchor: والنادي : المكان الذي ينتدي فيه الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r9.claim: The term applies to the meeting place only while its people are present; after they leave, it is no longer called a nādī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r9.anchor: ولا يقال للمجلس ناد إلا ما دام فيه أهله فإذا قاموا عنه لم يسم ناديا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r10.claim: The response parallels 29:24, where Lot’s people answer by demanding his death; the command to bring punishment is a challenge and implies that he had warned them of punishment during his mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r10.anchor: الكلام فيه كالقول في نظيره المتقدم آنفا في قوله { فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه } ( العنكبوت : 24 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r11.claim: Their command is meant to declare Lot powerless; it implies that he warned them of punishment, a normal part of prophetic preaching even though the earlier account omitted it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p240/r11.anchor: والأمر في { ائتنا بعذاب الله } للتعجيز وهو يقتضي أنه أنذرهم العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that he discussed “a-innakum” elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r1.anchor: تقدم القول في القرآن في أإنكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r2.claim: One group says highway robbery was widespread among Lot's people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة: كان قطع الطريق بالسلب فاشيا فيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they intercepted travelers to pursue sexual misconduct and terrorize them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: كانوا يقطعون الطرق على الناس لطلب الفاحشة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r4.claim: Another group takes this as cutting off procreation by abandoning women and having sex with men.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل أراد قطع سبيل النسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r5.claim: Another group says their infamous reputation made people avoid their roads and trade routes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أراد أنهم لقبح الأحدوثة عنهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r6.claim: “Nādī” means a gathering place; it is generic because cities have many such places, meaning wherever people assemble.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r6.anchor: و «النادي» المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r7.claim: One group says they pelted people with pebbles and mocked strangers; their gatherings lacked religion or propriety.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r7.anchor: فقالت فرقة كانوا يحذفون الناس بالحصباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r8.speaker: أم هاني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r8.claim: Umm Hāniʾ reports from the Prophet that they pelted and mistreated strangers; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives no grading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r8.anchor: أم هاني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد ومنصور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r9.claim: Mujahid and Manṣūr say they had sex with men in their assemblies while others watched.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومنصور: كانوا يأتون الرجال في مجالسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r10.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r10.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad says their indecency was sexual activity in their gatherings; al-Zahrawī transmits the view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r10.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد: منكرهم أنهم كانوا يتفاعلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they broke wind and slapped or clapped in their assemblies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس كانوا يتضارطون ويتصافعون في مجالسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r12.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r12.claim: Mujahid also lists pigeon play, henna on fingertips, whistling, pebble-throwing, and general shamelessness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: كان أمرهم لعب الحمام وتطريف الأصابع بالحناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r13.claim: Since some such acts occur among sinners in Muhammad's community too, mutual admonition against them is obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r13.anchor: وقد توجد هذه الأمور في بعض عصاة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فالتناهي واجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r14.claim: Lot's people answer his confrontation with denial and obstinacy, demanding punishment because they are convinced he is false.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r14.anchor: فلما وقفهم لوط على هذه القبائح رجعوا إلى التكذيب واللجاج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r15.claim: Their challenge means they think the punishment will not come and Lot cannot bring it; such defiance reflects settled disbelief in him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p314#3/r15.anchor: وهم لم يقولوا هذا إلا وهم مصممون على اعتقاد كذبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
