IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r1.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that they accosted travelers for their sexual offense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r1.anchor: أحدها أنهم كانوا يعترضون من مر بهم لعملهم الخبيث قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r2.claim: Muqatil says they threw stones at travelers from their gatherings, blocking the road.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أنهم كانوا إذا جلسوا في مجالسهم يرمون ابن السبيل بالحجارة فيقطعون سبيل المس قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi says they cut off reproduction by turning from women to men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه قطع النسل للعدول عن النساء إلى الرجال حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says النادي means an assembly or gathering place.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says munkar covers obscene speech and action.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r5.anchor: والمنكر يجمع الفواحش من القول والفعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r6.speaker: أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r6.claim: Umm Hani reports from the Prophet that one offense was pelting and mocking road travelers; Ikrima and al-Suddi say they pelted passersby.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r6.anchor: أحدها أنهم كانوا يحذفون أهل الطريق ويسخرون منهم فذلك المنكر روته أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب عن رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r7.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r7.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran reports from Ibn Abbas such acts as wrapping cloth on the hand, dragging garments, undoing buttons, pelting, playing with pigeons, whistling, and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r7.anchor: والثاني لف القميص على اليد وجر الإزار وحل الأزرار والحذف والرمي بالبندق ولعب الحمام والصفير في خصال أخر رواها ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r8.speaker: عروة عن عائشة والقاسم بن محمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r8.claim: Urwa reports from Aisha that the offense was flatulence; al-Qasim ibn Muhammad agrees.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r8.anchor: والثالث أنه الضراط رواه عروة عن عائشة وكذلك فسره القاسم ابن محمد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r9.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say it was men having sex with men in their gatherings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r9.anchor: والرابع أنه إتيان الرجال في مجالسهم قاله مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r10.claim: People should gather only for what brings them near to God, not mockery and play.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p268#3/r10.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أنه لا ينبغي للمجتمعين أن يتعاشروا إلا على ما يقرب من الله عز وجل ولا ينبغي ان يجتمعوا على الهزء واللعب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r1.claim: Lot rebuked his people for the unprecedented act of approaching men; they also disbelieved, denied their messenger, and opposed him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r1.anchor: في إتيانهم الذكران من العالمين، ولم يسبقهم إلى هذه الفعلة أحد من بني آدم قبلهم. وكانوا مع هذا يكفرون بالله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r2.claim: They intercepted travelers on the road, killing them and seizing their property.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r2.anchor: أي: يقفون في طريق الناس يقتلونهم ويأخذون أموالهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r3.claim: Mujahid says they publicly approached one another sexually in their gathering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r3.anchor: فمن قائل: كانوا يأتون بعضهم بعضا في الملأ قاله مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r4.speaker: عائشة والقاسم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r4.claim: Aisha and al-Qasim say their gathering's indecency included farting and laughing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r4.anchor: كانوا يتضارطون ويتضاحكون؛ قالته عائشة، رضي الله عنها، والقاسم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r5.claim: Another reported explanation is that they made rams butt one another and roosters peck one another; Ibn Kathir says they did worse things too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r5.anchor: ومن قائل: كانوا يناطحون بين الكباش، ويناقرون بين الديوك، وكل ذلك كان يصدر عنهم، وكانوا شرا من ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أم هانئ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r6.claim: In response to Umm Hani, the Prophet explains the indecency as assaulting people on the road and mocking them. Al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan and says it is known only through Hatim ibn Abi Saghira from Simak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r6.anchor: عن أم هانئ (1) قالت: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، عن قوله عز وجل: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r7.claim: Mujahid lists whistling, playing with pigeons and clay pellets, asking in the gathering, and unfastening robe collars as their other indecencies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} قال: الصفير، ولعب الحمام (7) والجلاهق، والسؤال في المجلس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276#2/r1.claim: Their demand for punishment if Lot was truthful showed disbelief, mockery, and obstinacy; Lot therefore prayed for help against the corrupt people, as stated in 29:30.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p276#2/r1.anchor: وهذا من كفرهم واستهزائهم وعنادهم؛ ولهذا استنصر عليهم نبي الله فقال: {رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين}

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r1.claim: This group makes the first إنكم declarative and the second أئنكم interrogative; the excerpt details their hamza variants.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب الأول بكسر ألف (إنكم) غير مستفهم (أئنكم لتأتون الرجال) مستفهم،

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وقالون عن نافع وزيد عن يعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Qalun from Nafiʿ, and Zayd from Yaʿqub use one lengthened hamza.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r2.anchor: فأبو جعفر وقالون عن نافع وزيد عن يعقوب بهمزة واحدة ممدودة

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and Yaʿqub are also reported with one unlengthened hamza.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r3.anchor: وابن كثير ونافع ويعقوب بهمزة غير ممدودة

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Hafs use two hamzas, the first for ease and the second in its original form.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r4.anchor: وابن عامر وحفص بهمزتين، فالأول للتخفيف والثاني على الأصل.

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads both clauses as questions with one lengthened hamza.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالاستفهام فيهما جميعا بهمزة واحدة ممدودة

JISHUMI:v8p5560/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r6.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r6.claim: ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read both clauses as questions with two hamzas.
JISHUMI:v8p5560/r6.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي بالاستفهام فيهما بهمزتين

JISHUMI:v8p5564/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r3.claim: Lewd conduct is more grotesque and vile when committed openly in the assembly.
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (في ناديكم المنكر) أنه في المجالس أشنع وأقبح.

JISHUMI:v8p5564/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r7.claim: The sexual immoralities were acts originated by the people themselves, refuting the Mujabbira doctrine that God creates human acts.
JISHUMI:v8p5564/r7.anchor: وتدل على أن تلك الفواحش كانت فعلهم حادثة من جهتهم، فيبطل قول المجبرة في المخلوق [*].

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r1.claim: The question means: do you have sexual relations with men?
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r1.anchor: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال } أي تنكحون الرجال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says they robbed travelers by cutting off the road.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنه قطع الطريق على المسافر , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara says their sexual crimes deterred people from traveling for fear of their vile conduct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنهم بإتيان الفاحشة من الرجال قطعوا الناس عن الأسفار حذرا من فعلهم الخبيث , حكاه ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r4.speaker: وهب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r4.claim: Wahb says they cut off offspring by turning from women to men, having made do with men instead of women.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r4.anchor: الثالث : أنه قطع النسل للعدول عن النساء إلى الرجال , قال وهب : استغنوا عن النساء بالرجال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r5.speaker: عائشة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r5.claim: Aisha says they passed gas in their gatherings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r5.anchor: أحدها : هو أنهم كانوا يتضارطون في مجالسهم , قالته عائشة رضي الله عنها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet, narrated by Umm Hani, says they pelted passersby and mocked them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r6.anchor: أنهم كانوا يخذفون من يمر بهم ويسخرون منه روته أم هانىء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r7.claim: Mujahid says they had sex with men in their gatherings; Mansur transmitted this report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r7.anchor: الثالث : أنهم كانوا يجامعون الرجال في مجالسهم , رواه منصور عن مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r8.claim: Mujahid's broader list includes whistling, pigeon play, catapults, lesbianism, and singing girls' garments being undone in gatherings; al-Hakim transmitted it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p281/r8.anchor: الرابع : هو الصفير ولعب الحمام والجلاهق والسحاق وحل أزرار القيان في المجلس , رواه الحاكم عن مجاهد .

MUJAHID:v2p494#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p494#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p494#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the wrongdoing in their gathering was that men came to them for sex.
MUJAHID:v2p494#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر ﴾ يعني في مجالسهم

MUQATIL:29:27-30/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r5.claim: Cutting the road means assaulting travelers: Lot’s people threw stones and clods at passersby from their meeting place.
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r5.anchor: يعنى المسافر، وذلك أنهم إذا جلسوا فى ناديهم، يعنى فى مجالسهم

MUQATIL:29:27-30/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r6.claim: The wrongdoing in their assembly means throwing stones at people.
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r6.anchor: يعنى فى مجالسكم المنكر، يعنى الحذف بالحجارة

MUQATIL:29:27-30/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r7.claim: When Lot forbade indecency and wrongdoing, his people demanded the punishment he said was coming in this world.
MUQATIL:29:27-30/r7.anchor: حين نهاهم عن الفاحشة والمنكر، { إلا أن قالوا } للوط، عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r1.claim: Cutting the road means killing and taking property, as highway robbers do.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r1.anchor: بالقتل وأخذ المال كما هو عمل قطاع الطريق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r2.claim: Another view is that they intercepted travelers to commit sexual wrongdoing against them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r3.claim: Nādī means an assembly or meeting place, and is called a gathering only while its people are present.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r3.anchor: مجلسكم ولا يقال للمجلس ناد إلا مادام فيه أهله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r4.claim: The condemned public acts include flatulence, sex, insults and obscenity in joking, flicking pebbles, chewing gum, finger-snapping, and using a toothstick among people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r4.anchor: أي المضارطة والمجامعة والسباب والفحش في المزاح والحذف بالحصى ومضغ العلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r5.claim: Instead of answering Lot, his people demanded God's punishment if he was truthful about its coming.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r6.speaker: شامي وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r6.claim: The Shami readers and Hafs read the opening with two hamzas, as in the canonical codex.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r6.anchor: أئنكم شامى وحفص وهو الموجود في الإمام وكل واحدة بهمزتين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r7.speaker: كوفي غير حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r7.claim: The Kufis other than Hafs lengthen the hamza and follow it with a kasra yāʾ.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r7.anchor: كوفي غير حفص آينكم آينكم بهمزة ممدودة بعدها ياء مكسورة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r8.speaker: عمرو ومكي ونافع غير قالون وسهل ويعقوب غير زيد
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r8.claim: The passage assigns the shortened-hamza form followed by a kasra yāʾ to Amr and the named Makki, Nafiʿ, Sahl, and Yaqub readers, with the stated exceptions.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p257/r8.anchor: أو عمرو أينكم أينكم بهمزة مقصورة بعدها ياء مكسورة مكي ونافع غير قالون وسهل ويعقوب غير زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r3.claim: The reading discussion for this phrase and the account of Lot and his people are treated earlier in al-Aʿrāf and Hūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r3.anchor: تقدم القراءة في هذا وبيانها في سورة «الأعراف». وتقدم قصة لوط وقومه في «الأعراف» و«هود» أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd explains cutting off the road as highway robbery.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r4.anchor: قيل: كانوا قطاع الطريق قاله ابن زيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.speaker: ابن شجرة
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.claim: Ibn Shajara says they seized people on the roads to commit the sexual offense with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r5.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يأخذون الناس من الطرق لقضاء الفاحشة حكاه ابن شجرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih interprets it as ending procreation by preferring men to women.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنه قطع النسل بالعدول عن النساء إلى الرجال قاله وهب بن منبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.claim: The author suggests all these crimes may have coexisted: they robbed and assaulted travelers and dispensed with women.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r7.anchor: قلت: ولعل الجميع كان فيهم فكانوا يقطعون الطريق لأخذ الأموال والفاحشة، ويستغنون عن النساء بذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.claim: Al-nādī means an assembly or council; interpreters differed over the wrongdoing practiced there.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r8.anchor: النادي المجلس واختلف في المنكر الذي كانوا يأتونه فيه فقالت فرقة:

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.speaker: أم هانئ
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.claim: Umm Hāniʾ reports the Prophet explaining that Lot’s people pelted passersby with pebbles and mocked them; al-Ṭayālisī recorded it, and al-Naḥḥās, al-Thaʿlabī, al-Mahdawī, and al-Māwardī cite it.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r9.anchor: وروته أم هانىء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.speaker: معاوية
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits Muʿāwiya’s report from the Prophet: each man kept pebbles ready, and a hit passerby was taken for the sexual offense.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r10.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي قال معاوية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r11.speaker: عائشة وابن عباس والقاسم ابن أبي بزة والقاسم بن محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r11.claim: ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿAbbās, and the two al-Qāsims say they farted in their assemblies.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r11.anchor: وقالت عائشة وابن عباس والقاسم ابن أبي بزة والقاسم بن محمد: إنهم كانوا يتضارطون

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r12.claim: Mujāhid, through Manṣūr, says they had sex with men openly in their assemblies while others watched.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r12.anchor: وقال منصور عن مجاهد كانوا يأتون الرجال في مجالسهم وبعضهم يرى بعضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r13.claim: Mujāhid also lists pigeon play, hennaed fingertips, whistling, pebble throwing, and shameless conduct generally.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r13.anchor: وعن مجاهد: كان من أمرهم لعب الحمام وتطريف الأصابع بالحناء والصفير والخذف

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some of these practices occur among sinners in Muḥammad’s community, so forbidding wrongdoing is obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r14.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد توجد هذه الأمور في بعض عصاة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فالتناهي واجب.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r15.speaker: مكحول
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r15.claim: Makḥūl lists ten Lot-like traits in this community: gum chewing, hennaed fingertips, loosened waistcloths, finger cracking, wrapped turbans, interlacing, galāhij throwing, whistling, pebble throwing, and liwat.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r15.anchor: قال مكحول: في هذه الأمة عشرة من أخلاق قوم لوط: مضغ العلك، وتطريف الأصابع بالحناء

QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists their other sins: injustice, insults, public farting, pebble throwing, backgammon and chess, dyed clothes, animal fights, cross-dressing, and levies on travelers; they also committed shirk and introduced liwat and lesbianism.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:28-29/r16.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: إن قوم لوط كانت فيهم ذنوب غير الفاحشة، منها أنهم يتظالمون فيما بينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r1.claim: After Lot confronted their vices, they returned to denial and obstinacy; demanding punishment implied they believed it could neither happen nor be brought about.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r1.anchor: فلما وقفهم لوط عليه السلام على هذه القبائح رجعوا إلى التكذيب واللجاج فقالوا:

QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r2.claim: Their challenge shows they were settled in the belief that Lot was lying; the author says such a statement is not natural for a mere obstinate challenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r2.anchor: وهم لم يقولوا هذا إلا وهم مصممون على اعتقاد كذبه. وليس يصح في الفطرة أن يكون معاند يقول هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r3.claim: Lot called on his Lord, who sent angels to punish them; they first visited Abraham to announce Lot’s victory over his people, as discussed in Hūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:29/r3.anchor: ثم استنصر لوط عليه السلام ربه فبعث عليهم ملائكة لعذابهم، فجاؤوا إبراهيم أولا مبشرين بنصرة لوط على قومه،

NASHR:v2p343/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p343/r8.claim: The author refers readers to earlier discussions of the disputes on إنكم لتأتون, the arrival of Abraham's messengers, and لننجينه وإنا منجوك; he also points back to the treatment of سيء.
NASHR:v2p343/r8.anchor: وتقدم اختلافهم في إنكم لتأتون من باب الهمزتين من كلمة
